what: Reaching the very end of the page and staying there: a 2px bottom bar fills from the left in 2s (cubic-bezier(1,-.01,.02,1) — it fills sharply near the end), and when full the bar wipes off to the right end in 1s while the text on the panel disappears in .5s, the gray panel sticks to the top of the screen, and a small next card in the center grows to fill the panel in 1.2s before moving on to the next page. Scrolling up even slightly before it fills rewinds the bar and cancels the transition — a transition that joins the end of a work detail to the first photo slot of the next work

options.dwell: Hold time at the end (s) = Bar fill length, default 2
options.grow: Seconds for the card to grow to fill the panel, default 1.2 — moves on when done
options.fade: fade: how long children take to vanish (seconds), default .5
options.leave: Length (s) over which the full bar clears to the right, default 1
options.bar-ease · leave-ease: Bar curve (four numbers like ”1,-0.01,0.02,1” or a CSS name), default 1,-0.01,0.02,1 · 0,0.27,0.13,1
options.to: Destination URL — if none, the card’s href, if that’s missing too, the first a[href] inside
options.ratio · ratio-narrow: Aspect ratio the panel or card takes when enlarged (wide window · 768 and below). If absent, the panel’s current ratio is used. Matched to the next page’s first photo ratio (reference site phone 1).
options.[data-fx-part=panel]: Board holding the cards — position: absolute inside the element; Set to bottom: 0. When it grows, the top edge sticks to the top of the screen
options.[data-fx-part=card]: Next card in the center of the panel — grows to fill the panel
options.[data-fx-part=fade]: (if present) text that disappears before growing (‹Next› title · card name)
options.fx:grow: Event the element emits when the bar is full and starts to grow — the consumer stops smooth scrolling (lenis.stop)
options.fx:next: Event fired when fully grown (detail.to, cancelable) — those using Barba or swup call preventDefault and trigger their own transition

note: Reaching the end means document height − 1 ≤ scroll + screen height. It is checked only through scroll events (even if it is already at the end on open, it must be scrolled once to start) — same as the original. Not attached under reduced motion (it does not advance by itself — cards remain as links). The plate is treated as an element that fills the screen and reaches the end, and is pinned above the screen
